literal: When Rong died the hundred officials entered to congratulate; Xinzhi alone received labor and inquiry.
idiomatic: After Rong's death the court came to congratulate; only Xinzhi was singled out for praise and questioning.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang died at Jinyang, Xinzhi feared within.
idiomatic: Xiaozhuang's death at Jinyang filled Xinzhi with dread.

literal: When Prince Xianwu of Qi raised the standard in Hebei, Xinzhi rushed to join him.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan, Prince Xianwu of Qi, rose in Hebei, Xinzhi hurried to his banner.

literal: In the time of the deposed emperor he was made scattered cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and right chief clerk to the Grand Chancellor.
idiomatic: Under the deposed emperor he became scattered cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and right chief clerk to the Grand Chancellor.

literal: At the start of the departing emperor's reign he inherited the former fief as founding baron of Ankang and was made General Who Pacifies the Army and regional inspector of North Xuzhou.
idiomatic: When the departing emperor took the throne he resumed the Ankang barony and became General Who Pacifies the Army and inspector of North Xuzhou.

literal: He went straight to his province; Fan Zihu held Xiqiu in revolt, and on the road he was killed.
idiomatic: Taking the direct road to his post, he met Fan Zihu's rebellion at Xiqiu and was slain on the way.

literal: For dying in the sovereign's service he was posthumously made bearer of the staff, commander of Ding and Yin, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Works, regional inspector of Dingzhou, posthumous name Wen Zhen.
idiomatic: Dying in royal service, he was posthumously bearer of the staff, commander of Ding and Yin, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Works, inspector of Dingzhou, styled Wen Zhen.

literal: Xinzhi's younger brother Qingluan, late in Wuding, was adviser to the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Younger brother Qingluan ended Wuding as adviser in the Minister of Works.

literal: Qingluan's younger brother Qingzhe died as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Granary and was posthumously made General of the Central Army and regional inspector of Jizhou.
idiomatic: Qingzhe, Qingluan's younger brother, died as vice director of the imperial granary and was posthumously General of the Central Army and inspector of Jizhou.

literal: His son Changyuan inherited.
idiomatic: Son Changyuan succeeded.

literal: In the Wuding era he was chief clerk of South Qingzhou.
idiomatic: In Wuding he was chief clerk of South Qingzhou.

literal: When Qi received the mandate the noble ranks were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: When Qi took the throne fiefs were lowered by rule.

literal: Yu's younger brother Pusa was a palace attendant.
idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Pusa served as palace attendant.

literal: On his death he was posthumously made governor of Jinan.
idiomatic: At death he was posthumously governor of Jinan.

literal: Tuwán's younger brother Zhongkui died young.
idiomatic: Tuwán's younger brother Zhongkui died young.

literal: The eldest son Fashou was palace attendant and central retainer, and rose to grandee of the central retainer.
idiomatic: Eldest son Fashou was palace attendant and central retainer, then grandee of the central retainer.

literal: He went out as General of the Dragon and regional inspector of Anzhou.
idiomatic: He left court as General of the Dragon and inspector of Anzhou.

literal: Fashou first sent trusted men in plain dress to enter the province and observe custom; as soon as he took office he rewarded and punished on a large scale, and the territory became orderly.
idiomatic: Before taking his post Fashou sent intimates in disguise to study local ways; on arrival he punished and rewarded sharply, and the province grew quiet.

literal: When his term ended and he returned, officials and people went to the gate to plead that he stay; Suzong praised this and ordered him back to the province.
idiomatic: At term's end the people petitioned at court for his return; Suzong approved and sent him back.

literal: He was later summoned as Grand Master of the Palace and given the added rank General of the Left.
idiomatic: He was recalled as Grand Master of the Palace with added General of the Left.

literal: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: He rose to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

literal: At the start of Jianyi he was killed at Heyin and posthumously made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and regional inspector of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: In the opening of Jianyi he died at Heyin and was posthumously Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and inspector of Xiangzhou.

literal: His son Qing Shi was aide in the Court of the Imperial Granary.
idiomatic: Son Qing Shi was aide in the imperial granary court.

literal: He was killed at the same time as his father.
idiomatic: He perished together with his father.

literal: Posthumously he was General of the Front and regional inspector of Guangzhou.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was General of the Front and inspector of Guangzhou.

literal: Qing Shi's younger brother Qingzun, late in Wuding, was cavalry commandery marshal of Yingzhou.
idiomatic: Qing Shi's younger brother Qingzun ended Wuding as Yingzhou's cavalry marshal.

literal: Qingzun's younger brother Qingzhi was handsome in appearance and had talent for desk work.
idiomatic: Qingzun's brother Qingzhi was fair of face and skilled at paperwork.

literal: He was assistant in the History Office and army adjutant to the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He served as History Office assistant and army adjutant under the Minister of Works.

literal: He died as chief clerk to the Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: He died as chief clerk to the Grand Preceptor.

literal: Fashou's younger brother Faseng rose from adjutant to the Grand Preceptor to direct-palace gentleman, General Who Pacifies the Distance, Secretariat and Marshal's adjutant, General of the Dragon, and regional inspector of Yizhou.
idiomatic: Younger brother Faseng advanced from adjutant to the Grand Preceptor through direct-palace gentleman, General Who Pacifies the Distance, posts under the Secretariat and Marshal, General of the Dragon, to inspector of Yizhou.

literal: He had never had governing ability; added to greed and cruelty, he killed at will and raged without constancy.
idiomatic: He lacked all capacity to govern; greedy and brutal, he killed as he pleased and raged without measure.

literal: Families Wang, Jia, and other leading clans of the province—Faseng called them all into the ranks as soldiers and showed no leniency.
idiomatic: Leading families Wang, Jia, and others—Faseng drafted them all as soldiers and granted no mercy.

literal: Then the whole province rebelled and called in outside enemies.
idiomatic: The whole province rose and invited foreign foes.

literal: Xiao Yan sent General Zhang Qi with a host to press the attack; the city gates stayed shut by day and travelers could not pass.
idiomatic: Xiao Yan's general Zhang Qi led troops against him; gates stayed closed by daylight and the roads were cut.

literal: Faseng memorialized: "I am shamed to guard a distant border; trouble arose beyond my foresight; bandits swagger and are strong wherever they stand."
idiomatic: Faseng wrote: "I guard a distant march in shame; rebellion flared beyond my planning; the enemy swells proud and strong on every side."

literal: Every garrison in the commandery has fallen; the people of neighboring provinces have also risen in disorder.
idiomatic: Every fort in the province is lost; neighboring districts have joined the revolt.

literal: Only the provincial seat still stands; the hour of destruction is not morning but evening.
idiomatic: Only the capital of the province remains; ruin comes not at dawn but at dusk.

literal: I reflect that I am already a dead man, yet I fear I cannot answer for my guilt before the court; as one of the imperial line I have deeply shamed the house.
idiomatic: I count myself dead already, yet fear I cannot answer at court; as imperial kin I have shamed the clan sorely.

literal: If I die a ghost I shall forever lose the heavenly countenance; under the nine springs the regret is very deep.
idiomatic: As a ghost I shall never again see the throne; in the grave my remorse runs deep.

literal: Now I send envoys by secret paths to run and report; if the court army comes swiftly, I may yet hope to be preserved whole.
idiomatic: I send messengers by hidden routes to beg aid; if the imperial host hurries, I may yet be saved.

literal: Weeping as I sent off the envoy, I know not what I said.
idiomatic: I wept as the messenger departed and scarcely know what I wrote.

literal: Suzong's edict said: "I lately ordered Fu Shuyan to march day and night, yet he has not arrived; send another capable gentleman of the Masters of Writing by post to urge him on, that we may lift them from hanging upside down and rescue this peril."
idiomatic: Suzong replied: "I already ordered Fu Shuyan to double his march, yet he has not come; send another able Masters of Writing officer by relay to hurry him, to end their torment and save the crisis."

literal: Shuyan repeatedly broke Zhang Qi, and the province was thereby preserved.
idiomatic: Shuyan routed Zhang Qi again and again, and the province was saved.

literal: Faseng was summoned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, went out as General Who Pacifies the East and regional inspector of Yanzhou, then General Who Pacifies the East and regional inspector of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: He was recalled as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, then General Who Pacifies the East and inspector of Yanzhou, then the same rank at Xuzhou.

literal: In the first year of Xiaochang Faseng killed the touring commissioner Gao Liang,[2] rebelled at Pengcheng, styled himself with a reign title, and named his era Heavenly Inception.
idiomatic: In Xiaochang year 1 Faseng killed touring commissioner Gao Liang,[2] rebelled at Pengcheng, took a royal title, and proclaimed the era Heavenly Inception.

literal: When the great army came against him, Faseng took his sons, seized the people of the city and the civil and military officials, and fled south to Xiao Yan.
idiomatic: The imperial host marched; Faseng carried off his sons, the city folk, and officials, and fled south to Xiao Yan.

literal: Zhongkui's younger brother Du, styled Acheng.
idiomatic: Zhongkui's younger brother Du, courtesy name Acheng.

literal: He was right leader of the crown prince's guard, commander of the Central Palace Guard, commander at Fuming garrison, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: He was right leader of the crown prince's guard, Central Palace Guard commander, commander at Fuming, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North and regional inspector of Youzhou.
idiomatic: He left as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Youzhou.

literal: On his death his posthumous name was Zhen.
idiomatic: His posthumous name was Zhen.

literal: The eldest son Hao, styled Hongda.
idiomatic: Eldest son Hao, courtesy name Hongda.

literal: He was chief clerk to the Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: He served as chief clerk to the Grand Preceptor.

literal: Ta's younger brother Hun succeeded his uncle Prince Lian of Guangping.
idiomatic: Ta's younger brother Hun succeeded his uncle, Prince Lian of Guangping.

literal: Hun's younger brother Bilin in the fifth year of Taiyan was made Minister of Works and granted the dukedom of Zangke.
idiomatic: Hun's brother Bilin in Taiyan year 5 became Minister of Works and Duke of Zangke.

literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and commander at the Huaihuang garrison.
idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and commander at Huaihuang.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Tianju inherited.
idiomatic: Son Tianju succeeded.

literal: In Gaozu's time he was General Who Subdues the Barbarians and regional inspector of Qingzhou.
idiomatic: Under Gaozu he was General Who Subdues the Barbarians and inspector of Qingzhou.

literal: He followed the emperor on the southern campaign, was made General of the Rear, then reduced from duke to marquis and made commander of the Western Palace Guard.
idiomatic: He followed the southern campaign, became General of the Rear, was lowered from duke to marquis, and made Western Palace Guard commander.

literal: In Shizu's time,[3] he was General Who Subdues the Barbarians and regional inspector of Xiazhou.
idiomatic: Under Shizu[3] he was General Who Subdues the Barbarians and inspector of Xiazhou.

literal: On his death he was posthumously given his former general's rank and made regional inspector of Jizhou.
idiomatic: At death he was posthumously general at his last rank and inspector of Jizhou.

literal: His son Yanbo inherited.
idiomatic: Son Yanbo succeeded.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Prince Yao of Henan was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianxing.
idiomatic: Prince Yao of Henan received his fief in Tianxing year 6.

literal: At five he once shot a sparrow before Taizu and hit it; Taizu marveled.
idiomatic: At five he shot a sparrow before Taizu and struck it; Taizu was astonished.

literal: When grown his martial skill was unmatched; with Prince Xi of Yangping and others he drilled the armies, and all bowed to his courage.
idiomatic: Grown, his martial arts were unrivaled; drilling with Prince Xi of Yangping and others, all acknowledged his valor.

literal: In the seventh year of Taichang he died, aged twenty-two.
idiomatic: He died in Taichang year 7 at twenty-two.

literal: He had seven sons.
idiomatic: He had seven sons.

literal: The eldest, Ti, was fierce and bold with his father's manner.
idiomatic: Eldest son Ti was fierce like his father.

literal: In Shizu's time he inherited the title and was re-enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan.
idiomatic: Under Shizu he succeeded and was made Prince of Yingchuan.

literal: He welcomed the honored consort from beyond the frontier at sixteen; he had early maturity, and the far regions revered him.
idiomatic: At sixteen he fetched the honored consort from the northern marches; precocious in judgment, distant lands honored him.

literal: Later his fief was changed to Wuchang.
idiomatic: His fief was later changed to Wuchang.

literal: He was made bearer of the staff, General Who Guards the East, and commander-in-chief at the Pingyuan garrison.
idiomatic: He received the staff as General Who Guards the East and commander at Pingyuan.

literal: Ten years in office, his renown stood very high.
idiomatic: In ten years of command his fame grew great.

literal: Later with Prince Ta of Huainan he pacified the Tujing rebel Hu, was promoted bearer of the staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, commander-in-chief at Tongwan, and was given a hundred horses and a thousand sheep—greatly favored.
idiomatic: With Prince Ta of Huainan he subdued the Tujing rebels, then became bearer of the staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, commander at Tongwan, with a hundred horses and a thousand sheep—deeply favored.

literal: In the first year of Tai'an he died, aged forty-seven; his posthumous name was Prince Cheng.
idiomatic: He died in Tai'an year 1 at forty-seven, posthumous name Prince Cheng.

literal: The eldest son Pingyuan inherited the title.
idiomatic: Eldest son Pingyuan succeeded.

literal: Loyal and resolute, with stratagem.
idiomatic: He was loyal, resolute, and resourceful.

literal: In Emperor Xianzu's time the Ruru raided the frontier; following the campaign, Pingyuan's battle merit was greatest.
idiomatic: When Xianzu marched against Ruru border raids, Pingyuan's share of the victory was largest.

literal: He was made acting bearer of the staff, commander of Qi and Yan, General Who Guards the South, regional inspector of Qi, skilled in winning hearts; more than a thousand frontier families submitted.
idiomatic: Made acting bearer of the staff, commander of Qi and Yan, General Who Guards the South, and inspector of Qi, he won people well; over a thousand frontier households came in.

literal: In Gaozu's time the sorcerer Sima Xiaojun called himself heir of Jin, gathered more than three thousand men, encamped at Pingling, and named his era Holy Lord.
idiomatic: Under Gaozu the wonder-worker Sima Xiaojun styled himself heir of Jin, mustered three thousand men at Pingling, and proclaimed the era Holy Lord.

literal: They stormed commanderies and counties and killed the chief officials.
idiomatic: They overran districts and slew their magistrates.

literal: Pingyuan personally campaigned, killed seven men, captured Xiaojun, and sent him to the capital for execution.
idiomatic: Pingyuan led the strike himself, slew seven, seized Xiaojun, and sent him to the capital to be beheaded.

literal: Another wonder-worker, Liu Ju, called himself Son of Heaven and stirred the people.
idiomatic: Another sorcerer, Liu Ju, proclaimed himself Son of Heaven and roused the folk.

literal: He campaigned again and beheaded him.
idiomatic: Pingyuan campaigned once more and cut him down.

literal: Grain failed that year and the people of Qi starved; Pingyuan gave three thousand-odd bushels of his private grain as porridge to save their lives.
idiomatic: When harvest failed and Qi went hungry, Pingyuan gave more than three thousand bushels of private grain as gruel to keep the people alive.

literal: More than a thousand northern garrison soldiers returning home were all given travel rations.
idiomatic: He supplied road grain to over a thousand northern garrison troops heading home.

literal: The people all praised him in song.
idiomatic: The people sang his praise everywhere.

literal: More than a thousand men of Qi, led by Han Ningzhi and others, went to court to acclaim him; Gaozu read their petition and sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: Over a thousand Qi subjects led by Han Ningzhi petitioned at court in his praise; Gaozu read it and marveled.

literal: Jian, styled Shaoda.
idiomatic: Jian, courtesy name Shaoda.

literal: In youth he had his father's manner and read widely in books and records.
idiomatic: Young, he bore his father's spirit and read widely.

literal: Grave and sparing of speech, broad and kindly toward gentlemen.
idiomatic: He was heavy and quiet, open-handed with scholars.

literal: He was made direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, soon given the added rank Champion General, and made intendant of Henan.
idiomatic: He became direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, soon Champion General as well, and intendant of Henan.

literal: When the imperial carriage marched south to conquer, Jian was made General Who Pacifies the South; on return he was made General of the Left Guard, then went out as General Who Subdues the Barbarians and regional inspector of Qi.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign he was General Who Pacifies the South; returning, General of the Left Guard, then General Who Subdues the Barbarians and inspector of Qi.

literal: At the start of institutional reform every measure was new; Jian above followed Gaozu's intent and below took Qi custom, his regulations bright and all within rule.
idiomatic: As institutions were remade, Jian upheld Gaozu's will above and Qi practice below; his ordinances shone and all fit the standard.

literal: Gaozu read what he submitted and admired it long, then turning to his attendants said, "If every regional inspector could be like this, changing customs would be no great matter."
idiomatic: Gaozu read his memorials, praised them at length, and told his attendants, "Were every inspector thus, reforming the land would be easy."

literal: An edict praised him and published it through the realm, exactly as Jian had written.
idiomatic: An edict commended him and circulated his words empire-wide.

literal: The people of Qi loved to sing of it, all saying their eyes and ears were renewed.
idiomatic: Qi folk sang of it, saying sight and hearing had been made new.

literal: After Gaozu's death, He abandoned the monkhood and returned to lay life, cast off wife and children, and took the widow Lady Cao as wife.
idiomatic: After Gaozu died, He left the clergy, forsook wife and children, and married the widow Lady Cao.

literal: Lady Cao was already advanced in years; she brought five sons and daughters with Jian to Licheng and meddled in government.
idiomatic: Lady Cao was old; she followed Jian to Licheng with five children and disturbed the administration.
